docs.presetsCoats.component: The stock coat recipes, each on its own page and its own knob. A coat is a RUNTIME layer over a
surface — `Atoms/Coated` teaches the atom and its reach; this shelf answers the narrower question:
what does `wash`, `ring`, `fill` or `censor` already look like, and what does its `level` do.
The recipes differ by the KIND of mark, never by value — an overlay, a stroke, a clipped fill, a
mask — so a darken and a charge are one `wash` told apart by tint and level. `clear` draws nothing
by itself, so its page shows it at work: stopping a cast cascade so a spotlight can light one
docs.presetsCoats.wash: A flat colour over the whole surface, opacity from `level`. The continuum lives here: a mana shard
charging, a figure dimming as it loses HP, a frozen tray greying — one recipe, and the magnitude is
the parameter. Drag `level`, pick a `tint`; there is no scene per value and no record per colour.
docs.presetsCoats.ring: A stroke around the contour, its weight growing with `level` — a selection ring, a ward. It is a
stroke, so it stands in for the surface's own border while it lasts: one stroke per quad.
docs.presetsCoats.fill: The blueprint completing: a SOLID coat over `level` of the face, bottom-up, cut off where the level
stops. A different KIND of mark from `wash` — a half-built thing is half DRAWN, not half faded —
and the hard cut edge is what says so. The fraction becomes clip points in the plan, where a unit
test reads them; the painter only obeys a mask.
docs.presetsCoats.clear: The recipe that draws NOTHING — its whole job is to STOP a cast. The tray casts a wash over both
tiles; the right one carries `clear`, so the nearest-cast walk stops there and the tile stays lit.
«All but this one» is a dim on the tray and a `clear` on the exception — overriding an inherited
docs.presetsCoats.censor: The hidden face GROUND UP. Motes are born on the node's own silhouette, each one carrying the
colour of the spot it came from; they drift outwards, fade in and out over their own short lives
and are replaced. A censored ace of spades still reads as an ace of spades, smeared — which is the
whole difference between a censor and a grey rectangle.
No GPU is involved: the motes are plain drawn squares, so there is no shader tier to fall back
from. The atom holds the static truth — `censor`, a strength — and where a mote is at second `t`
is a pure function under a unit test. Drag `level`: the cloud thickens.
docs.presetsCoats.foil: A cold streak sliding down the diagonal — and the slide IS the edition: a laminated sheet is dull until the light moves on it. So the recipe names a SHADER, the painter builds it and the shared clock drives it.

What stays flat is only what survives without one: a pale film and the bright hairline round the edge. A rim runs along the contour, which a filter over the face cannot own, so it is a stroke and stays one.
docs.presetsCoats.polychrome: The iridescent one: a single hue, a little different at every point of the face and at every moment. That drift is what iridescence IS, and there is no honest flat stand-in for it — cut into slices it read as a flag rather than as oil on water.

So the recipe NAMES a shader and hands it a place on the wheel, which is where `tint: {token:"spin", param}` goes. The light itself lives in `render/pixi.ts`, the one file that owns pixels; the single flat film left behind is the fallback for a backend whose program will not build, not the look.
docs.presetsCoats.glass: See-through and blurred, on the shader the censor already clocks. What makes it glass rather than a censor is that it barely tints and keeps a bright rim: what is under it stays readable.
docs.presetsCoats.frost: Glass without the rim - the soft pane a dialog puts over the table behind it. Its own recipe rather than a flag on glass, because a flag would be a sort for a reader to guess at.
docs.presetsCoats.faded: Barely there. Toward the DESK rather than toward a colour, because that is what a viewer means by transparent - a coat cannot make the surface beneath it see-through, however it is named.
